title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page finishes a proof begun on the previous page, states a corollary, and states a new lemma.

**End of the proof of Lemma 1 (Lucas's theorem).** Write c_{ij} = (i+j)!/(i!j!) and i = u + pr, j = v + ps with 0 ≤ u, v ≤ p-1.
- The previous page handled the case u+v ≤ p-1 by expanding (X+Y)^{i+j} = (X^p+Y^p)^t (X+Y)^w in F_p[X,Y], where t = r+s and w = u+v. This gives c_{ij} ≡ c_{u,v} c_{r,s} (mod p).
- This page closes the case w = u+v ≥ p. No monomial X^iY^j occurs, so c_{ij} ≡ 0. Applied to (u,v) in place of (i,j), the same argument gives c_{u,v} ≡ 0. Hence the product formula holds in all cases.
- Induction on the length of the p-adic expansions then gives the full Lucas formula c_{ij} ≡ ∏ c_{u_ε,v_ε} (mod p). It also gives the Kummer-type criterion: c_{ij} ≢ 0 iff the digit sums u_ε+v_ε never exceed p-1, i.e. there are no carries.

**Corollary 2.** Suppose N+1 ≡ 0 (mod p) and write N+1 = (N'+1)p, so N = N'p + (p-1). The p-adic digits of N+1 are those of N'+1 shifted by one place. The digits of N are p-1 followed by those of N'. For ε ≥ 1 the corollary states:
- c_{N+1,p^ε-1} ≡ c_{N'+1,p^{ε-1}-1} (mod p). This is ≡ 1 if p^{ε-1} divides N'+1 and ≡ 0 otherwise.
- c_{N,p^ε} ≡ c_{N',p^{ε-1}} ≡ v_{ε-1}+1 (mod p), where N' = Σ v_α p^α.

The proof applies Lucas, using that p^ε-1 has ε digits all equal to p-1. One gets c_{N+1,p^ε-1} ≡ ∏_{k=0}^{ε-2} c_{u_k,p-1}, and each factor is nonzero iff u_k = 0. Similarly c_{N,p^ε} ≡ c_{v_{ε-1},1} = v_{ε-1}+1.

**Lemma 2 (statement only).** Let Z_(p) be Z localized at p, E a Z_(p)-module, N ∈ ℕ, and e ≥ 0 with p^e ≥ N+1. Let I = {N} ∪ {N+p^ε : 0 ≤ ε ≤ e}. Take a family (x_i)_{i∈I} in E with binom(j,i)(x_j - x_i) = 0 for i = N, N+1 and every j ∈ I with j > i. The conclusion (on the next page) is x_N = x_{N+1}.

The next page proves this as follows. Set y_ε = x_{N+p^ε} - x_N. The hypotheses become c_{N,p^ε} y_ε = 0 and c_{N+1,p^ε-1}(y_ε - y_0) = 0. Pass to the weaker mod-p system and induct on N via N → N' = (N+1)/p - 1. Corollary 2 is exactly the tool that makes this descent work.

**Margin remark.** For an F_p-module one cannot conclude that all x_i are equal. The example is p = 2, e = 2, N = 2, so I = {2,3,4,6}. Then binom(3,2) = 3 and binom(6,2) = 15 are odd, while binom(4,2) = 6, binom(4,3) = 4 and binom(6,3) = 20 are even. Hence x_2 = x_3 = x_6, but x_4 is unconstrained.

**Purpose.** The coefficients binom(j,i) are those of x^{[i]}x^{[j-i]} = binom(j,i) x^{[j]}. So Lemma 2 is evidently a technical step about divided-power (PD) polynomial algebras in the PD de Rham complex lectures. A plausible use is showing that a function or class compatible with PD multiplication is determined, or constant, in consecutive degrees. The exact use is unsure from this page alone.
errors: Minor: Lemma 1 is said to follow 'du corollaire' by induction; the reduction step meant is the displayed statement (*) from the previous page. This is a naming slip, not a mathematical one.
In Corollary 2 the parenthetical '(≡1 si ε=1)' attached to the first line correctly reflects the empty product. No mathematical error was found in the congruences; they check against Lucas's theorem.
The margin remark's phrasing is a cautionary counterexample: it shows the conclusion cannot be strengthened to x_i = x_N for all i. It does not assert that such a strengthening holds.

ideas.what: Lucas's theorem: c_{ij} ≡ ∏ c_{u_ε,v_ε} (mod p), with c_{ij} ≢ 0 iff there are no carries, proved by expanding (X+Y)^{i+j} in F_p[X,Y]
Mod-p values of binom(N+p^ε, N) and binom(N+p^ε, N+1) when p divides N+1, by shifting p-adic digits from N to N' = (N+1)/p - 1
Lemma 2: binomial-weighted relations binom(j,i)(x_j - x_i) = 0 on the index set {N} ∪ {N+p^ε} force x_N = x_{N+1}; proved by induction on N via p-adic digit shifting
ideas.modern_name: Technical lemma on divided-power coefficients (integrality / triviality in PD polynomial algebras)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (standard-type arguments in crystalline cohomology, e.g. Berthelot)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a textbook proof of Lucas's theorem, a straightforward corollary, and the statement of a technical lemma about binomial relations among divided-power coefficients. All of it is correct and careful, but elementary; there is nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'récurrence immédiate sur la longueur e des développements p-adiques écrits de u et de v': the image more likely reads 'longueur ν' (the letter used for expansion length on the previous page), and 'u et de v' probably refers to the expansions of i and j.

Margin remark: the image reads roughly 'Rem. si E un F_p-module, [on ne] peut [pas] conclure que x_i = x_N ∀ i ∈ I (ex. p=2, e=2, N=2, donc x_2, x_3, x_4, x_6; on a x_2=x_3=x_6 mais pas x_4=x_6)'. This is consistent with the computation.
